This compound is directly linked to 3-oxoacyl-[acyl-carrier-protein] synthase 3, which in turn is targeted by beta-Tocotrienol and Coenzyme A. The latter is known to interact with the IgG receptor FcRn large subunit p51, indicating a possible role in the cellular processing of immunoglobulins. The integration of these targets suggests that 12S,13S-Hydroxyandrographilide may influence the function of FcRn through its interaction with downstream metabolic intermediates, potentially modulating the receptor's activity. The evidence highlights a mechanistic link between the compound and the receptor, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
